topics.title: PHP security flaw keeps sites patching
topics.summary: A serious PHP vulnerability has prompted urgent patching and precautionary website outages worldwide. Cybersecurity officials say the issue affects a language used by a large share of the web.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a familiar website goes offline, are you patient, do you hunt for a workaround, refresh too often, or decide it is fate telling you to do something offline?

topics.title: Astronomers revisit Starry Night's sky
topics.summary: A new study suggests Van Gogh's Starry Night may reflect a real July 1889 dawn, though museum experts say the case for the painting's established June dating remains stronger.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you could time-travel to watch one artist at work for an hour, who would you choose, and would you be helpful or just stand there trying not to breathe loudly?

topics.title: Bridget Jones prize seeks new comedy voices
topics.summary: Author Helen Fielding has launched a 1,000-word comedy-writing prize for unpublished writers in northern England, with support and cash awards intended to spotlight fresh voices.
topics.discussionPrompt: What tiny everyday mishap could you turn into a great comedy scene: losing keys, a disastrous group chat, cooking confidence, awkward neighbours, or a shopping trip gone sideways?

topics.title: Four cities make culture shortlist
topics.summary: Blackpool, Sheffield, Milton Keynes and Wrexham have been shortlisted for UK City of Culture 2029. Each finalist will receive funding, while the winning city will receive a larger award.
topics.discussionPrompt: If your town hosted a year of culture, what would be its signature event: food festival, music trail, film night, public art, neighbourhood stories, or something wonderfully odd?

topics.title: Retailer sees tougher holiday spending
topics.summary: Sainsbury's says households remain under financial pressure as the holiday shopping season approaches, a sign that retailers are watching customer spending closely.
topics.discussionPrompt: What makes a holiday gathering feel generous without becoming expensive: a favourite dish, homemade decorations, games, swapping skills, a shared playlist, or a strict no-gift rule?

topics.title: UK energy debate returns to net zero
topics.summary: The UK government says it remains committed to net-zero targets after approving the Jackdaw gasfield, reopening discussion about how energy security, jobs and emissions can be balanced.
topics.discussionPrompt: When an energy choice involves bills, jobs and emissions, what question would you ask first? Is there a local solution you wish more people talked about?

topics.title: Brewer flags changing pub habits
topics.summary: Heineken has told British pubs that widespread use of weight-loss medicines could reduce demand for beer and cider, encouraging venues to consider smaller serves and alcohol-free options.
topics.discussionPrompt: What makes a pub, café or hangout feel welcoming if you are not drinking alcohol: good snacks, better music, games, comfy seats, fancy soda, or staying open late?

topics.title: Finnish data-centre project faces scrutiny
topics.summary: Finnish authorities halted work at proposed data-centre sites after environmental assessment concerns following extensive tree felling, fueling debate about the local costs of AI infrastructure.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a huge data centre came to your area, what would you ask about first: jobs, electricity, water, trees, taxes, or whether its heat could help nearby homes?

topics.title: Banana researchers explore hardier crops
topics.summary: Researchers are exploring breeding advances that may help protect Cavendish bananas from disease and climate pressures, raising hope for a fruit supply that has long relied on a narrow genetic base.
topics.discussionPrompt: If one everyday food suddenly became rare, which would disrupt your routine most? Would you happily try a new version, or start a dramatic campaign to save the original?

topics.title: Oil and markets react to global uncertainty
topics.summary: Oil reached a five-month high while global stocks wobbled, showing how energy worries and shifting expectations around technology can quickly change the mood in financial markets.
topics.discussionPrompt: When economic news feels abstract, what everyday clue makes it real for you: grocery prices, fuel, rent, a job search, travel costs, or something else?
